meta.linksNote: Checked on that date, not guaranteed after it: a page that answered this morning can move or die tomorrow. The two that did not answer are neoped.eu and htfc-eu.com, both NXDOMAIN, and each is flagged on the event it belongs to. Four hosts refuse automated requests but are live in a browser, and were read there.

items: Cross-checked the five events marked green in Katka's 12-month calendar sheet against this board: Georgia Tech Pediatric Innovation Day, MEDICA 2026, WHX Tech 2027, NeoPed 2027 and The MedTech Forum 2027. All five were already here. Four of them needed correcting.

Georgia Tech, two corrections and one of them matters. There was no 2026 edition on 7 Jul 2026; that date was in the record with nothing behind it and is gone. The pitch now runs inside the Pediatric Healthcare Innovation Summit with iSPI, last held 5 to 6 Nov 2025 in Atlanta with applications closing 20 Jul 2025, and the pool is USD 80,000 from the FDA Pediatric Device Consortia. The gate: only companies based in the US, or holding a US office and a US taxpayer ID, are eligible for the cash. Consultation prizes are open to everyone. With no US entity, the cash is not currently winnable.

WHX Tech Xcelerate is not free after all. Applying costs nothing, but eligibility requires shortlisted startups to hold a confirmed WHX Tech Startup Pod, and Informa publishes no pod price. The route now says so rather than reading as a free shot at USD 30,000. Numbers corrected too: around 50 pitch, up to 40 shortlisted, 12 in the Grand Finale. Deadline unchanged at 4 Nov 2026.

WHX Tech's call for speakers closed on 28 Aug 2026 and is now marked closed. The page still displays as open and still dates the event to September 2027, while the landing page, the Xcelerate page and ABHI all say 27 to 29 January 2027. The flag stays until Informa fixes the page.

MEDICA's pitch deadline is unchanged at 10 Sep 2026, 23:59 CET, now 10 days out, and the prices are unchanged. Three eligibility gates are newly recorded: submissions in English only, nothing launched before 2023, and the solution must be available in at least one market by the end of Q2 2027. That last one is the real constraint for a TRL 4 simulator. The final is 17 Nov 2026 at 15:00 CET.
The MedTech Forum's 2027 registrations page is live and reads 'The registration fees will be available soon.' Dates and city re-confirmed: 10 to 11 May 2027, Rome.

NeoPed's site is still down. neoped.eu was NXDOMAIN on Google, Cloudflare and a third resolver, so it is the domain and not local DNS. The 2026 edition was real: 23 to 24 Apr 2026 in Berlin, with SIOP Europe as media partner. Nothing about 2027 can be verified while the site is dark.

Housekeeping caught by the link checker: HLTH Europe's old registration link (europe.hlth.com/register) is dead. Repointed to the become-a-sponsor enquiry form and the 2027 register-interest page, both live. Still no published rate. Separately, htfc-eu.com stopped resolving, so HealthTech Innovation Days now has the same problem NeoPed has.

Second pass, same day: every one of the 37 events had its primary source re-read, and all 115 links in the file were requested. 113 resolved. Everything now carries a 31 Aug 2026 stamp, and every stamp is backed by a page that was actually opened today.

Two organisers' sites are dark. neoped.eu and htfc-eu.com both return NXDOMAIN on Google's and Cloudflare's resolvers. htfc-eu.com is HealthTech Innovation Days, whose event is on 1 Oct 2026, one month out, so that one matters. Eurobiomed is the only live contact route left for it.

SWPDC is the correction that could have cost something. This board said the Fall 2026 prize round closed on 14 Aug 2026. It has not closed: applications are due Friday 7 Sep 2026 at 17:00 CST and the Apply Now link is live. The 14 Aug date belongs to a different competition, the five-consortium joint pitch, whose US-based and in-person-Boston conditions had also been copied onto the SWPDC record. Both removed. What SWPDC actually requires is that the technology meets the FDA definition of a medical device, which is still the blocker for a training device.

CRAASH Barcelona closes today. This record read '8th edition, dates not posted, unannounced'. Biocat publishes the 9th edition with a call running 29 Jun to 31 Aug 2026, interviews 21 Sep to 8 Oct, and a programme starting 26 Oct 2026 for five months. i4KIDS guarantees places for paediatric projects.

CEPAS was marked unannounced while its full rate card was published. Fixed: early 590 non-member and 450 member closed 31 Jul, regular 720 / 550 runs to 30 Sep, late 900 / 685 through October, all including 10 percent French VAT.

CTIP's grant is US-only. 'Only projects taking place in the US are eligible to apply for this grant.' The 2026 round ran 23 Mar to 1 May 2026 and is closed. That is now on the record, alongside the same restriction already noted for Georgia Tech's cash prizes.
Elevate has a Startup Pass at CAD 325, cheaper than the 450 General Admission this board was quoting, and restricted to startups rather than service providers. Now priced.
EUPSA has moved domain: eupsa.info 301s to eupsa.eu. Links repointed.
The SIM Expo open item is resolved. Two abstract deadlines were on record, 17 Apr and 13 Jul. The Simulation Canada page gives one: Friday 17 April 2026 at 5pm ET. The 13 Jul date is dropped.
The robotic surgery course has run. The 4th annual was 19 to 21 Aug 2026 in Columbus, registration having closed 12 Aug. No 5th annual is announced, so its figures stay marked prior-year.

Georgia Tech, root cause found. The phantom '7 Jul 2026 edition' was the date of an APDI press release announcing USD 25,000 prizes at the showcase, misread as the date of the showcase itself. The release carries no event date and no deadline, and nothing else publishes one.
The page now carries a link-check line: how many links resolved, when they were checked, and which hosts did not answer. Checked is not the same as guaranteed, and the wording says so.

Decisions are no longer trapped in one browser. Yes, Maybe and No lived only in localStorage, so they existed on the machine that set them and nowhere else, and the Plan tab came up empty anywhere else. An event can now carry a decision in the data file, which seeds the browser once per event and then never again, so anything changed or cleared by hand stays that way. The five events marked green in the 12-month calendar sheet (Georgia Tech, MEDICA 2026, WHX Tech 2027, NeoPed 2027, The MedTech Forum 2027) are seeded as Maybe. Note that the private notes read 'not worth attending' for Georgia Tech, so that one is a deliberate override.

Every event and every column was re-run against one question: does this event offer this opportunity? Where the answer is no the cell reads n/a with a link to what was checked. Where it is yes, the route now records who can take it and on what terms, the cost, when and how to register, and what you get out of it. All 108 routes across 148 cells now carry all four.
'Not applicable' is now just n/a.

A correction to my own dates. Everything checked in this session was stamped 26 August because that is what the previous build said, when the work actually happened on 28 August. 125 date mentions and every verified stamp are corrected. The two entries below dated 26 August are genuinely from that day.
WHX Tech's call for speakers closes today, 28 August 2026. It was previously described as two days out, which was wrong by exactly that error.

A Refresh button now sits above the table. It re-pulls the data file past your browser cache. It cannot re-read the organisers' sites from your browser, because this page is static with no server behind it, so a second button raises a re-check request carrying the rule above into the Sunday job.
validate.py now refuses any route missing conditions, how to register, or what you gain, so the rule is enforced rather than remembered.

Two errors Katka caught, both mine. Helsinki is free: the Eventbrite listing gives lowPrice 0.0, and it was showing as 'not published' because I read the organiser page instead of the ticket page. The lesson from MEDICA applied here too and I did not apply it.

Worse, the Helsinki 'Sponsor the day' row was invented. There is a general Become a sponsor invitation on the organiser page and no published offer behind it, so showing it as a live route with a hidden price was misleading. It now reads 'No exhibition found' with the reason.

Same audit run across every unpriced exhibition row. Nine are now evidenced with what was actually checked, and three had no published offer at all: Elevate, HTID and NeoPed now say so instead of implying one exists.

The Helsinki event does have a competition and we missed it. The Paediatric Hospital Innovation Challenge 2026 is closed with five hospital projects already selected. Note the eligibility: the call goes to paediatric hospitals for solutions built inside hospitals, so a company probably needs a hospital partner to enter. Expect the next call around the turn of the year.

Two real exhibition rates found while auditing. SESAM: EUR 3,500 excluding VAT for a 2x2 shell scheme, up to EUR 25,000 for Platinum, and Laerdal, Elevate Healthcare and Surgical Science all exhibit there. PHM: USD 3,000 a booth, with sponsorship over USD 6,000 including the space.
Everything already missed now records when to expect the next window, and why we think that. Seventeen closed routes carry an expected reopening tied to an observed prior cycle, not a guess.

The nearest ones to watch: MedTech Innovator around December 2026, the AdvaMed Call for Sessions in early January 2027, the next five-consortium pediatric round in spring 2027, and the IMSH 2028 Call for Content in spring 2027.
A Track checkbox was added to every row. Tracked events appear in a new Plan view in date order, and ticking the routes you intend to do adds the costs up.

Totals are kept separate by currency. No exchange rate is applied, because a made-up rate in a budget is worse than three honest subtotals. Routes with no published price are counted and flagged so the total reads as a floor, not a forecast.

Katka's correction taken: where registration is actually open, the rates are usually one click into the booking flow rather than on the landing page. Chasing MEDICA into the Messe Duesseldorf shop produced real numbers: a visitor day ticket is EUR 50, the four-day season ticket EUR 150, Premium EUR 799. It had been sitting as 'not published'.

The last six unanswered Present cells are closed. EAPS and HLTH USA do run calls and both have shut for this edition. HTID, NeoPed, the MedTech Forum and the Nationwide robotic surgery course have no open call at all, and each now says why.
i4KIDS Helsinki venue corrected to Aalto University, Toolo Banquet Hall, from the Eventbrite listing. 18 September 2026, 09:00 to 16:00.
Costs now carry a machine-readable value and currency so the planner can add them up.
Every route now says what you get out of it, not just what it costs. That is a new field on all 89-plus routes and it shows in the expanded row.

Attend and exhibit are now answered for every event. Where a congress runs an exhibition but will not publish a rate, which is most of them, the cell says so and names who to ask instead of showing a blank.
Finland was missing a flag. Fixed.

Petra's 12-month calendar folded in. Corrections: the HLTH USA prize is 25,000 cash plus 25,000 in credit, not 25,000; NCC-PDI awards 150,000 to 250,000 in FDA grants across winners, far more than the 25,000 recorded; the EAPS simulation competition prize is free registration.

One conflict left standing rather than papered over: the UCSF-Stanford award reads as USD 100,000 platinum on the consortium site and up to roughly USD 50,000 per finalist in Petra's calendar. Both are on the record now.
Priority flags realigned to Petra's priority column, plus jENS, SAGES, Impact4Kids and the joint consortium round.
Katka's fit verdicts from that calendar stay in the private overlay, not on the public page.
Pitch routes now show what you can win next to what it costs to enter. Cost alone was only half the decision.

The comparison is unflattering in one case: MEDICA costs EUR 3,500 to get on the stage and the entire prize pool is EUR 3,500 in cash. That is a visibility spend, not a funding route, and it now reads that way on the page.

Biggest prizes on the board: MedTech Innovator USD 350,000 non-dilutive, the UCSF-Stanford PDC platinum award USD 100,000, WHX Tech Xcelerate USD 30,000 equity free, HLTH Europe EUR 30,000, HLTH USA USD 25,000.
The CIX Startup Awards at Elevate are a dead end and are now marked closed. The 2026 cohort of fourteen was named in February, and the award is for Canadian startups.
Impact4Kids pays nothing and takes nothing. Six places, six months, training and mentorship and EU-US immersion. Worth entering for the access, not the money.

Teach is no longer its own column. Running a hands-on course is a way of actively participating, so it folds into Present. Route labels already say which kind it is, for example the PAS Call for Workshops.

Events are now typed as conference, competition or accelerator, and the type can be filtered. Accelerators are not conferences but they are the same kind of visibility lever and they run on the same deadlines.

Impact4Kids 2026/27 added and marked priority. Applications close 27 September 2026. No cost, no equity, no funding: fortnightly training, one-to-one mentorship and immersion in both the EU and US ecosystems. Eligibility is TRL 3 to 6, Europe or US, under USD 5M dilutive raised, which InfantSim fits.

CRAASH Barcelona added. Biocat's three-month accelerator, and i4KIDS joined the 8th edition as paediatric partner with at least one place reserved for a paediatric project. Dates for that edition are not posted.
i4KIDS Pediatric Innovation Day, Helsinki, 18 September 2026 added. The showcase slots are already filled, but sponsorship is open, which is the cheaper way into the network that runs Impact4Kids.
Rows can now be starred as priority in the browser, and starred rows can be filtered on their own.
A validator now runs before every commit. On its first run it found the Europaediatrics link was dead, two organiser sites unreachable, and a schema slip of my own making.

Europaediatrics 2026 is fine, but its link was not. The old MCA page returns HTTP 410 Gone; the congress moved to an EventsAir portal and is still on for 8 to 10 October 2026 in Venice. Link replaced.

Two organiser sites would not answer at all on 28 Aug 2026: htfc-eu.com for HealthTech Innovation Days, and neoped.eu, which does not resolve in DNS. Both records now say so rather than implying they were verified at source. NeoPed should be treated as unconfirmed.
PAS 2027 was collapsing six separate calls into two vague rows. It is now broken out into the actual named calls from the PAS key dates table, each with its own window.

That surfaced a route worth having: the PAS Call for Workshops, 3 Aug to 16 Sep 2026, is the taught hands-on route and the closest fit at PAS for a simulator. It closes the same day as the scholarly sessions call.
Also added at PAS: the Call for APA and PAS Special Interest Groups, and the ancillary events window for running your own satellite session, which stays open to 3 Mar 2027.
Table cells now name the route. Previously a cell with two entries showed two costs and two countdowns with no way to tell which was which.

Four statuses were wrong because they were inferred from a missing date rather than read off the page. Katka caught the first one. Fixed, and a validator now runs before every commit so this class of error cannot ship again.

The MedTech Innovator route at The MedTech Conference said 'not announced'. The page names all 65 companies in the 2026 cohort and says the five finalists are set, so the round is closed. The way back in is the 2027 accelerator, tracked separately.

The MedTech Conference Call for Sessions said 'not announced'. It closed on 20 February 2026. The AdvaMed page still advertises it as open while naming a window that has passed, so the page copy is stale and is now flagged as such.
The UCSF-Stanford PDC pitch said 'not announced'. It is accepting applications now. That page is also internally inconsistent, advertising a 2026 round next to a 2025 event date.
WHX Tech Xcelerate now has a real deadline: applications close 4 November 2026, prize pool USD 30,000 equity free, split 15,000 / 10,000 / 5,000.

The WHX Tech date conflict is mostly resolved: the landing page and the Xcelerate page both say 27 to 29 January 2027, against one call-for-speakers page saying September 2027. January is the better supported date.
Calls for speakers are now tracked separately from academic abstract calls. They are a different route with a different gatekeeper, and five were being missed entirely.
WHX Tech has an open call for speakers that closes 28 August 2026, which is two days out. It is the most urgent thing on the board.

WHX Tech dates are in conflict between two Informa pages. The call-for-speakers page says September 2027 at the Dubai World Trade Centre; the WHX Tech landing page says 27 to 29 January 2027. Flagged on the record, unresolved.

Speaking at MEDICA is bought rather than submitted. A MEDICA connected healthcare forum slot is EUR 550 on top of a stand; the cheapest route to any stage is still the EUR 3,500 START-UP PARK package.
Exhibit pricing found and added: AAP National Conference USD 3,800 per 10 x 10 plus USD 200 per corner, and PAS USD 3,500 per 10 x 10 from the 2026 prospectus.

MEDICA standard stand costed out at EUR 4,983 for the smallest permitted 12 sqm row stand, all compulsory fees included. That is about 70 percent more than the START-UP PARK package for the same show.
Exhibit routes added for The MedTech Conference, HLTH USA and SAGES. None publish a rate; each now names who to ask instead of showing a blank.
Five events added: the joint five-consortium Pediatric Device Pitch Competition, SAGES 2027, LSI USA '27, SESAM 2027 and the CTIP Catalyzing Pediatric Innovation grant.

The SWPDC and AAP SOATT prize is no longer a standalone prize. It is now one joint round run with APDI, CTIP, MPDC and the UCSF-Stanford PDC, it closed on 14 August 2026, and eligibility requires a device meeting the FDA definition plus a pediatric indication for use. The record is marked closed.

SAGES 2027 Emerging Technology is the notable new opening: it accepts industry engineers and inventors presenting their own work, with no formal experimental data required. The window runs 15 Sep to 4 Nov 2026.

Two startup competitions were being missed. The MedTech Conference hosts the MedTech Innovator Finals, USD 350,000 non-dilutive, and IMSH hosts the SimVentors Showcase, which is restricted to technology that is not yet commercially available.
Every event now says explicitly whether a startup competition exists. Where none was found, the cell says so and links to what was checked, rather than showing a blank.
The MEDICA pitch cost was understating it. The stage slot is not sold separately, so the real cost to pitch is EUR 3,500: the EUR 2,950 booth plus the EUR 550 stage upgrade.
Every route now carries its own link to more information, and the table cells are clickable.
The SIM Expo hotel block is logistics, not a way to take part, so it no longer appears in the closing-deadline rail.
The card view is gone. The table is the only event view.
Adding an event is now a single link field.

Ways to take part are now five named routes rather than four generic ones: present, pitch, attend, exhibit and teach. Abstract became present. The hands-on pre-congress courses at IPEG and EUPSA were sitting under exhibit and are now their own teach route.

Every route now carries a cost with a source link, and a basis flag saying whether the figure is published for this edition, carried over from the previous edition, approximate, free or simply not published.
HealthTech Innovation Days 2026 is confirmed for 1 October 2026 in Paris. It was previously logged as an estimate of early to mid October.
The MedTech Forum 2027 is confirmed for 10 to 11 May 2027 in Rome. The host city was previously unannounced.
Georgia Tech Pediatric Innovation Day ran on 7 July 2026, so the record was pointing at a date that had already passed. It now tracks the 2027 cycle.
APSA 2027 call for abstracts is still not posted, which now makes it more than a year late against the 2026 pattern. Checked again 28 Aug 2026.
MedTech Innovator 2027 applications have still not opened. The 2026 cohort closed and only a waitlist is live.

New routes added: attend and teach for APSA 2027, attend for IPEG 2027 and EUPSA 2027, a pre-conference course route for IMSH 2027, a pre-congress course for jENS 2027, exhibitor tier for the Nationwide Children's robotic surgery course, and visitor entry for MEDICA 2026.
jENS 2027 abstracts: the 31 March date is 2027, not 2026. Submission opened 21 July 2026 and closes 31 March 2027, so this is open now.
IMSH 2027 Call for Content closed 27 May 2026. The SimVentors Showcase is 25 January 2027 and excludes commercially available technologies.
SWPDC and AAP SOATT prize: the consortium states eligibility is limited to devices going through the FDA regulatory pathway. 2026 round still unannounced.
UCSF-Stanford PDC: the accelerator is stated as restricted to US-based applicants. Award size is up to 100K USD, not 50K. Runs twice a year.
MedTech Innovator: the 2026 cohort closed 1 December 2025, earlier than the 16 December recorded. The window has moved earlier two years running.
MEDICA competitions confirmed at 10 September 2026, 23:59 CET. MEDICA states no MDR or FDA conformity is required to enter.
IPEG 2027 confirmed as 27 to 30 April in Naples, in collaboration with ESPES and SICP. Abstract details still pending.
APSA 2027 call not yet posted. The 2026 guide appeared in August of the preceding year, so it is due imminently.
First build of the radar from the tracker sheet: 29 events, 62 ways to participate.
Deadline status computed live against today's date rather than typed by hand.

events.name: SWPDC + AAP SOITT Pediatric Device Prize
events.org: Southwest-Midwest PDC (Texas Children's / Baylor) with AAP SOATT
events.where: Virtual application; consortium in Houston, TX
events.summary: Fall 2026 prize round from the Southwest-Midwest National Pediatric Device Innovation Consortium and the AAP Section on Innovation in Therapeutics and Technology. Up to USD 25,000. Application is a short questionnaire, an itemised budget and an optional 1 to 2 minute video pitch.
events.audience: Pediatric medical device innovators at any stage.

participate.label: Apply for the prize
participate.note: Applications opened 28 Jul 2026 and the Apply Now link is live. Outcome notified in September 2026.

cost.detail: No entry fee. Up to USD 300,000 across the round, up to USD 50,000 per project. Closed for the Fall 2026 round.

prize.detail: Up to USD 25,000 in prizes across the round. Funds may be used for regulatory and IP consultants, engineering design, prototyping and manufacturing, study equipment and supplies, clinical trial expenses and personnel. Six-monthly progress reports required.

participate.gain: Up to USD 25,000 non-dilutive, plus the SWPDC virtual accelerator relationship behind it.
participate.conditions: Exactly three criteria are published: open to pediatric device innovators, the technology must be a Medical Device as defined by the FDA, and it must benefit the pediatric patient population as the FDA defines it, age 21 or younger. The FDA-device test is the one that bites: InfantSim is a training device, not an FDA-classified medical device. Note that no US-residency requirement is published on this page, unlike the joint five-consortium pitch.
participate.how: Apply through swpdc.org/aapsoitt by Friday 7 Sep 2026, 17:00 CST. Short questionnaire, itemised budget from their template, and an optional 1 to 2 minute video pitch, which they encourage. Scored on Significance, Innovation and Feasibility.
participate.checked: 2026-08-31: corrected at source. This record said the Fall 2026 round closed on 14 Aug 2026. It did not. The SWPDC page reads 'Applications are due by Friday, September 7th, 2026 at 5:00 p.m CST' with a live Apply Now link. The 14 Aug 2026 date belongs to a different competition, the five-consortium joint pitch at pedsinnovation.org, whose US-based and in-person-Boston conditions had also been copied onto this record. Both removed. Eligibility here is the three criteria the page actually lists.

events.name: Elevate Festival 2026 + CIX Startup Awards
events.where: Downtown Toronto, Ontario
events.summary: Canada's largest tech festival, housing the CIX Startup Awards and investor-pitch program with a health-innovation category.
events.audience: Founders and investors. CIX curates startups before 600+ investors and 94+ North American judges.

participate.label: Attend the festival

cost.detail: Startup Pass, the relevant tier for a founder, excluding tax. General Admission is 450, Investor 750, Trailblazer 1,500, all excluding tax and all shown against higher list prices. The Startup Pass is restricted to startups and tech ventures: service providers, consultants, government bodies and contract R&D must buy General Admission. A subsidised ticket can be requested through a form if cost is a barrier.

participate.gain: Access and meetings. No platform and no speaking slot, so value depends entirely on who you line up first.
participate.conditions: Open to anyone, but the cheap tier is not. The Startup Pass at CAD 325 is limited to startups and tech ventures scaling a product, and includes founder programming and investor meetings through Meeting Exchange. Service providers, consultants, government organisations and contract R&D firms are told to buy General Admission at 450 instead.
participate.how: Buy at elevatefestival.ca/tickets. Startup Pass CAD 325, General Admission 450, Investor 750, Trailblazer 1,500, all excluding tax, and priced to rise. Subsidised tickets on request.
participate.checked: 2026-08-31: read off the ticket page in a browser, which blocks automated fetches. Startup Pass 325, GA 450, Investor 750, Trailblazer 1,500, all excluding tax. This record previously gave only a GA band of 450 to 550 and did not price the Startup tier, which is the cheaper one and the one InfantSim would use.

participate.label: CIX Startup Awards pitch
participate.note: Watch cixsummit.com.

cost.detail: CIX Startup Awards entry terms and any fee for the 2026 round are not posted.

prize.detail: Recognition and a stage at the CIX Summit in front of 600-plus investors, not money. Two blockers: the 2026 cohort of fourteen was already named in February 2026 from over 370 applications, and the award is explicitly for Canada's top startups, so a Slovak company is very unlikely to be eligible.

participate.checked: 28 Aug 2026: fourteen 2026 winners were announced in February 2026, selected by 94 North American investors from over 370 applications. Framed throughout as an award for Canadian startups.
participate.gain: Stage time in front of investors and buyers, plus whatever the prize carries.

expect.basis: The 2026 cycle closed 30 Nov 2025 and winners were named in February 2026. Note the bigger blocker: the award is for Canadian startups, so the cycle may not matter.

participate.conditions: Effectively Canada-only: the award is framed throughout as recognising Canada's top startups, and all fourteen 2026 winners are Canadian. A Slovak company is unlikely to qualify.
participate.how: Applications for the 2026 cohort closed 30 Nov 2025 and winners were announced in February 2026, judged by 94 North American investors from over 370 applications. Watch cixsummit.com around November for the next cycle.

participate.label: Become a speaker
participate.note: Elevate runs an open Become A Speaker route on its speakers page. No deadline is published; the line-up is updated on a rolling basis.

cost.detail: No speaker fee published.

participate.gain: A named slot in the programme, and the clinical or academic credibility that comes with being selected rather than buying your way in.
participate.checked: 28 Aug 2026: the speakers page carries an open Become A Speaker route. No deadline and no fee are published, and the line-up is updated on a rolling basis.
participate.conditions: Open submission, no stated restriction on company stage or nationality.
participate.how: Through the Become A Speaker route on the festival speakers page. No deadline is published and the line-up is filled on a rolling basis, so earlier is better.

absentWhy.exhibit: Elevate sells sponsorships as a festival but publishes no exhibition or booth offer, and the CIX awards route is closed and Canada-only anyway.

events.name: EAPS 2026
events.where: Megaron Athens International Conference Centre, Athens
events.summary: Large multidisciplinary European paediatric and neonatal congress with hands-on simulation sessions. Now a commercial event after the 2025 EAPS/CEPAS split.
events.audience: Paediatricians, neonatologists, nurses, researchers, trainees.

participate.label: Attend

cost.detail: Non-member early rate, to 24 Jun 2026. Member EUR 510. Regular 750 / 600 to 18 Aug, onsite 850 / 680. Nurse or early career investigator 320 / 260 early. Online-only 320.

participate.gain: Access and meetings. No platform and no speaking slot, so value depends entirely on who you line up first.
participate.conditions: Open to all. Cheaper rates apply to members of collaborating societies, nurses, early career investigators, pharmacists, physiotherapists and students, each needing status confirmation at registration.
participate.how: Register at eaps.kenes.com/register. The early rate closed 24 Jun 2026 and the regular rate closed 18 Aug 2026, so only the onsite tier remains for the 24 to 27 Sep 2026 congress. A Flex Pass at EUR 55 lets you switch between in-person and online.
participate.checked: 2026-08-31: re-read eaps.kenes.com. 24 to 27 September 2026, Athens and online, unchanged. The 18 August 2026 registration savings deadline has passed, and the site now reads 'Onsite registration rates & Online participation still available', so you can still attend at the onsite rate of 850 non-member or 680 member. This route is marked closed for the savings window, not for attendance.

participate.label: Team Simulation Competition
participate.deadlineLabel: Entry deadline not published. Needs verifying.
participate.note: Winning team gets free registration.

cost.detail: Competition terms for 2026 not posted. No separate entry fee published.

prize.detail: The winning team gets free congress registration. No cash.

participate.gain: Stage time in front of investors and buyers, plus whatever the prize carries.
participate.checked: 28 Aug 2026: entry deadline still not published. Per Petra's 12-month calendar, read 28 Aug 2026 the winner receives free registration, and the competition is run for teams of doctors and nurses on a high-fidelity paediatric manikin.
participate.conditions: Built for teams of doctors and nurses working a high-stakes case on a high-fidelity paediatric manikin. It is a clinical team contest, not a company showcase, so a device maker enters only by supplying or partnering with a clinical team.
participate.how: Entry terms and deadline are not published. Ask Kenes via the congress site. The winning team receives free congress registration.

participate.deadlineLabel: Space sold until the hall fills

cost.detail: The exhibition is confirmed to exist, the rate is not published. Ask Kenes ILS industry team, price list on request.

participate.gain: Floor presence and demo time in front of the people who specify and buy training equipment. For a physical simulator this is the only route where they get their hands on it.
participate.checked: 28 Aug 2026: a Download Price List page exists for industry, so a rate card is prepared, but the figures sit behind the request.

cost.detail: No submission fee. Presenters pay standard registration, shown at the non-member early rate.

participate.gain: A slot in a large multidisciplinary European paediatric and neonatal programme.
participate.checked: 28 Aug 2026: abstract guidelines page live, but the presenting-author deadline of 24 Jun 2026 has passed.

expect.when: Around spring, for the next edition
